sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Academic Research Skills (ARS) is a suite of Claude Code skills for academic research, from planning a paper through literature review and drafting to publication. It keeps you in charge, pausing for your confirmation at every stage.
sixtySeconds.problem: AI writing tools can invent citations and push researchers out of the decisions. ARS handles grunt work like finding references and formatting citations, adds integrity checks such as citation verification, and stops for your approval at each step.
whoFor: Graduate students and academics writing papers
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a human-in-the-loop research pipeline with integrity gates, citation anchors and an optional claim audit, built for Claude Code and available for other hosts.
requirements: Optional: Pandoc for DOCX, tectonic for PDF

overview: Install it as a Claude Code plugin, then run /ars-plan to map a paper's structure through Socratic dialogue, or /ars-lit-review for a one-shot literature review. It also works on claude.ai and Claude Desktop paid plans as a plugin added from a repository, though hooks and plugin agents don't run in plain chat there.

The pipeline includes integrity gates with a blocking checklist of known AI research failure modes, locator anchors on every citation and an opt-in claim audit (ARS_CLAIM_AUDIT=1) that checks each cited source. Style Calibration learns your voice from past work.

The README estimates about US$3 to 7 in model costs for a full 15,000-word paper at 2026-09 list prices. Sibling distributions exist for Codex CLI and Pi. ARS is licensed CC BY-NC 4.0, which does not allow commercial use.
